title: Prove the routed-reply warnings on transcript fixtures
action: Test only, no product code. Write transcript event fixtures in both the Claude shape (assistant tool_use Bash + user tool_result + assistant text) and the Codex shape (response_item function_call + function_call_output + message). Cover: orient with principles and a reply with no slug (warns); same with a slug (quiet); same with 'no principle changed anything' (quiet); orient with a situation line and a Read of .claude/skills/bee-planning/playbooks/bugfix/bug-fix.md (no playbook warning); orient with a situation line and no playbooks read (playbook warning); orient in an earlier turn than the last user message (quiet); no orient (quiet). Drive the Stop hook entry end to end where the existing session_close tests do, and assert it never blocks. Show each new test red against a mutation. A red against the product is a finding returned as blocked. Bee commands you may run: none beyond the verify. Run no dispatch verb, not even its help.

truths: a test fails if the principle warning fires on a reply that names a slug
a test fails if the playbook warning misses a turn that opened no playbook
a test fails if either warning blocks the Stop
